reigns.note: Pausanias' first king of the land then called Actaea; Apollodorus and Hyginus instead begin the line with the earth-born Cecrops.
The autochthonous man-serpent, or (Pausanias) son-in-law of Actaeus; in his reign Athena and Poseidon contested the land.
Another son of the soil; in his reign the flood of Deucalion fell. Expelled by Amphictyon.
Son of Deucalion or another autochthon; reigned twelve years, then expelled by Erichthonius.
Earth-born of Hephaestus, reared by Athena; founded the Panathenaea and set up the wooden image of the goddess.
In his reign Demeter and Dionysus came to Attica; father of Erechtheus, Butes, Procne and Philomela.
Won the war with Eleusis but was destroyed by Poseidon (or Zeus' thunderbolt) for slaying Eumolpus.
Eldest son of Erechtheus; succeeded after Poseidon destroyed his father's house.
Driven out by the sons of Metion; fled to Megara, married Pylia, and became king there.
The sons of Metion usurped the throne during Pandion II's exile; Pandion's sons returned from Megara and expelled them.
Eldest of the four restored Pandionids, he took the whole power; childless until Theseus.
Son of Aegeus (or Poseidon); slayer of the Minotaur, unifier of Attica, the great Athenian hero-king.
